Science.title: Mapping the uncharted plate tectonic cycle: The hidden path from plate destruction to new oceanic crust

Meanwhile, magma continuously rises from the deep mantle to form new oceanic crust, erupting as mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB).

Science.title: Giant lambda-shaped stellar nursery found in the Milky Way's outskirts
Science.summary: Massive stars often form in dense regions, called "hubs," where filamentary structures made of star-forming materials meet. These star-forming complexes are "hub-filament" systems. Astronomers have discovered one such large network of molecular gas filaments in the outer regions of the Milky Way. It is called the λ-complex, and the structure is bigger than most known hub-filament systems. The research paper was published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society on Nov. 17.

Science.title: Errors in judging friendships predict who will connect or drift apart six months later
Science.summary: Decades of research show that mental representations of social networks are riddled with errors, with people commonly misidentifying existing ties and reporting relationships that do not exist. While these inaccuracies have been interpreted as noise arising from the limits of memory or attention, Brown University researchers have discovered a much more intriguing explanation: These "errors" are accurate representations of social connections that just haven't happened yet.

Science.summary: During animal development, the establishment of the three primary body axes—head-to-tail (anterior-posterior), dorsal-ventral and left-right—is essential for building a proper body structure. Science.title: Einstein’s 120-year-old theory may be missing something big about the Big Bang

Their new calculations show that heavy quarks moving through an ultra-hot plasma experience rare but unusually powerful jolts that Einstein’s traditional model cannot fully explain.

Science.title: Draining peatlands leaves a long legacy of warming
Science.summary: Peatland ecosystems like bogs and swamps perform an important balancing act: Their vegetation takes up huge amounts of carbon dioxide, while their soil microbes produce methane. Although methane is a potent greenhouse gas, peatlands exhibit a net cooling effect on the planet because of the sheer scale of carbon dioxide they remove from the atmosphere, which has amounted to hundreds of gigatons globally over thousands of years.

Science.title: Physicists just sent an unblockable message through a brick wall using gravity
Science.summary: Scientists have successfully transmitted a message through a brick wall using nothing but gravity, an old elevator, and an incredibly sensitive detector. By moving a massive counterweight between two positions, researchers encoded the word "Gravity" into tiny changes in gravitational pull. Unlike Wi-Fi or radio signals, gravity passes through ordinary barriers without being blocked, offering a potentially revolutionary way to communicate.

Science.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists

Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter. Team will conduct most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Any difference between the electron and positron could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics.
